newsitem.title: USA: IDEC says drug eased arthritis symptoms.
newsitem.headline: IDEC says drug eased arthritis symptoms.

text.p: IDEC Pharmaceuticals Corp and SmithKline Beecham Pharmaceuticals said Monday that patients in a Phase II trial showed "clinically significant improvement" in arthritis symptoms when treated intraveneously with the IDEC-CE9.1/SB 210396 antibody.
Patients experienced minimal side effects, no adverse infusion-related events were reported, and prolonged depletion of CD4+ T cells did not occur, they said.
Results of the Phase II trial were presented on October 19 at the annual meeting of the American College of Rheumatology held in Orlando, Fla.
The antibody is being jointly developed by the two companies.

The results are based on 122 patients who received either 40 mg, 80 mg or 140 mg intravenous doses of IDEC-CE9.1/SB 210396 or an intravenous placebo in the Phase II trial. The doses were administered twice weekly over a four-week period.
In the 140 mg, 80 mg and 40 mg groups, the median time to clinical response was one week, two weeks and two and a half weeks, respectively.
Treatment of the 140 mg group was discontinued after patients developed rashes. That was not observed in the other groups.
Clinically significant treatment response was experienced by 77 percent of the patients in the highest dosage group, 47 percent in the 80 mg group, and 42 percent in the 40 mg group.
In the placebo group, 17 percent of the patients experienced a clinically significant treatment response.
